title: Affine group action stackification equals the torsor stack without smoothness
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be an affine group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $V$ be any $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a left action $a:G\times_k V\to V$. No smoothness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed on $G$ or $V$. Use universes [def-weil-size-convention] and the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $\mathcal A$ be the stackification [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] of the action groupoid, with objects $x:T\to V$ and arrows $g:x\to y$ given by $g\in G(T)$ such that $a(g,x)=y$. Let $\mathcal T(T)$ have objects pairs $(P,f)$ where $P\to T$ is a scheme with a left $G_T$-action fppf locally isomorphic to $G_T=G\times_kT$ with left translation, and $f:P\to V$ is $G$-equivariant. Its arrows are equivariant $T$-isomorphisms commuting with $f$, and pullback is by fibre product. Then $\mathcal T$ is an fppf stack and the trivial-torsor functor extends to a pullback-compatible equivalence $\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal T$. This functor sends $x$ to $(G_T,(h,t)\mapsto a(h,x(t)))$ and sends $g:x\to y$ to right translation $h\mapsto hg^{-1}$. A stack means a category fibred in groupoids with sheaves of isomorphisms and effective descent for objects [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. All torsors here are schemes, rather than just algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), situation-quotient-stack and lemma-group-quotient-stack-in-groupoids, with no smoothness hypothesis. Scheme torsors for affine G: spaces-descent.tex Tag 041Z (lemma-descending-property-affine), descent.tex Tag 0245 (lemma-affine).

proof.text: Affine effectivity available for the covering families used below. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-family-affine-effectivity-reduction] to the property that a scheme morphism is affine. Base-change stability is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). For finite coproduct stability, cover each target component by affine opens; each inverse image is affine, so the coproduct morphism is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target]. This also treats the empty coproduct. The affine flat surjective case is [lem-galois-affine-flat-descent-effective], which assumes only flatness and surjectivity, hence applies in particular with the finite-presentation hypothesis in the reduction lemma. Consequently every descent datum of affine scheme morphisms on an fppf covering is effective as a scheme. In particular the trivial torsors $G_U\to U$ are affine morphisms: they are base changes of the affine structural morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. No finite presentation of G is needed: the finite-presentation hypothesis in the reduction concerns the covering A to B, not the object being descended.

source.place: Tag 0245 (lemma-affine), first paragraph of proof and Tag 02W3 (lemma-descending-types-morphisms); morphisms.tex Tags 01S8 and 01SD.

proof.text: Isomorphisms in $\mathcal T$ form fppf sheaves. Given compatible local equivariant isomorphisms $P|_{U_i}\to Q|_{U_i}$, the family $P\times_TU_i\to P$ is an fppf covering. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] it is fpqc, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] glues these maps uniquely to a scheme morphism $P\to Q$. Apply the same assertion to the local inverses; the composites equal the identity because they do on the covering. The resulting isomorphism lies over $T$ and commutes with the maps to $V$ since those equations hold locally. Equivariance is equality of two maps $G_T\times_TP\to Q$, checked after its covering base change to the $U_i$ using the same uniqueness assertion. This proves both existence and uniqueness of glued arrows without any separation assumption on $Q$ or $V$.

source.place: Tag 0370 (lemma-group-quotient-stack-in-groupoids), omitted arrow-sheaf axiom expanded using descent.tex Tag 023Q and topologies.tex Tag 022C.

proof.text: Descend the underlying schemes of objects. Let $(P_i,f_i)$ and equivariant transition isomorphisms $\alpha_{ij}$ be a descent datum on an fppf covering $T_i\to T$. Choose fppf coverings $U_{ia}\to T_i$ trivializing $P_i$, and write $\lambda_{ia}:G_{U_{ia}}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_i|_{U_{ia}}$. Composing coverings gives an fppf covering of $T$. On $U_{ia}\times_TU_{jb}$ transport $\alpha_{ij}$ by the $\lambda$'s; these are scheme isomorphisms between the restrictions of $G_{U_{ia}}$ and $G_{U_{jb}}$. Their cocycle follows by cancellation of $\lambda$ and the cocycle of $\alpha$. Step 1 therefore supplies a scheme $P/T$ and compatible isomorphisms $P|_{U_{ia}}\simeq G_{U_{ia}}$. For fixed $i$, their composites with $\lambda_{ia}$ are compatible maps to $P_i$ over the covering $U_{ia}\to T_i$, since pulling the original transition along the diagonal $T_i\to T_i\times_TT_i$ gives the identity (the cocycle gives an invertible idempotent there). Glue them, and their inverses, by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] and [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. This gives $\eta_i:P|_{T_i}\simeq P_i$; the identities $\alpha_{ij}\eta_i=\eta_j$ follow after the refining covering, hence globally by uniqueness in the same lemma.

source.place: Tag 0370 (lemma-group-quotient-stack-in-groupoids), object descent; scheme effectivity supplied by descent.tex Tag 0245 instead of descent of algebraic-space torsors.

proof.text: Descend the remaining structure. Via $\eta_i$, the actions on $P_i$ give compatible maps from $(G_T\times_TP)|_{T_i}$ to $P$, and the $f_i$ give compatible maps from $P|_{T_i}$ to $V$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] these glue to $a:G_T\times_TP\to P$ and $f:P\to V$. The unit and associativity equations for $a$ hold after the coverings of $P$ and $G_T\times_TG_T\times_TP$ induced by $T_i\to T$, so hold globally by uniqueness in morphism descent. The same argument on $G_T\times_TP$ proves $f(a(g,p))=g\cdot f(p)$. On every $U_{ia}$ the constructed action is left translation under $P|_{U_{ia}}\simeq G_{U_{ia}}$; hence $P$ is a scheme torsor by the definition in the item. The $\eta_i$ are equivariant and commute with $f$, as checked on that covering. Thus the original datum is effective. Together with Step 2 this proves that $\mathcal T$ is a stack; fibre-product pullbacks give its cartesian lifts and groupoid fibres. In particular we never use the torsor projection itself as an fppf covering: it need not be locally of finite presentation when G is not of finite type.

source.place: Tag 0370 (lemma-group-quotient-stack-in-groupoids), descent of the equivariant map and omitted structural checks, using descent.tex Tag 023Q.

proof.text: Define the functor $F_p$ from the action groupoid by $x\mapsto(G_T,f_x)$ with $f_x(h,t)=h\cdot x(t)$ and $g:x\to y\mapsto R_{g^{-1}}$. Right translation commutes with left translation, and $f_y(hg^{-1},t)=h\cdot(g^{-1}\cdot y(t))=h\cdot x(t)$, so it is an arrow of $\mathcal T$. If $g:x\to y$ and $b:y\to z$, their composite is $bg$, and $R_{b^{-1}}\circ R_{g^{-1}}(h)=hg^{-1}b^{-1}=h(bg)^{-1}$; identities are also preserved. Each formula is unchanged by base substitution. Thus $F_p$ is a pullback-compatible functor on the associated fibred groupoid.

source.place: Tag 04WM (proposition-equal-quotient-stacks), construction of F_p and right-translation formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] on the big fppf site, with $\mathcal P$ the action fibred groupoid and $\mathcal Y=\mathcal T$. The site and its fibre groupoids are taken in the larger universe fixed in the big-site convention. Step 4 verifies the required stack hypothesis on $\mathcal Y$ and Step 5 verifies pullback compatibility. The universal-property clause supplies a pullback-compatible $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T$ and an invertible comparison $Fi\simeq F_p$. We use this comparison when identifying images of objects and arrows below.

source.place: Tag 04WM, extension of F_p using stacks.tex Tag 0436 (lemma-stackify-groupoids-universal-property).

proof.text: The functor $F$ is fully faithful. First take objects $i(x),i(y)$ from the action groupoid over $T$. The presheaf of $g\in G(U)$ with $g\cdot x|_U=y|_U$ is already a sheaf: compatible $g$ glue as maps $U\to G$ by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], and the equality in $V$ is local by the same morphism-uniqueness assertion. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] this is the isomorphism sheaf between $i(x)$ and $i(y)$. On the torsor side an equivariant isomorphism $r:G_U\to G_U$ has $r(h)=h\,r(e)$, hence is uniquely $R_{g^{-1}}$ for $g=r(e)^{-1}$. The compatibility $f_y r=f_x$, evaluated at $e$, is equivalent to $g\cdot x=y$; the converse follows from Step 5. These inverse descriptions commute with restriction. For arbitrary $\xi,\zeta\in\mathcal A(T)$, the same stackification node supplies a common refining covering on which both come from $x,y$. The map on isomorphism sheaves is thus bijective locally; local preimages of a target arrow agree on overlaps by the local injectivity, and glue uniquely because $\mathcal A$ is a stack. This proves bijectivity on each isomorphism set, globally.

source.place: Tag 04WM, full-faithfulness argument identifying the two Isom sheaves; local description from stacks.tex Tag 02ZP.

proof.text: Finally, any $(P,f)\in\mathcal T(T)$ has a trivialization $\lambda:G_U\simeq P|_U$ on an fppf covering. Put $x=f(\lambda(e))$. Equivariance gives $f(\lambda(h))=h\cdot x$, so $\lambda$ identifies the restriction with $F_p(x)$, hence with $F(i(x))$. Both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal T$ are stacks, $F$ is pullback-compatible by Step 6, and its fibres are fully faithful by Step 7. Therefore [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] gives the asserted equivalence over $k$, including a pullback-compatible inverse up to invertible natural transformations. Its arrow convention is the one of Step 5. The argument used affineness of $G$ solely to descend the trivial torsor schemes in Step 3 and imposed no finiteness, affineness or separatedness condition on $V$. Thus neither smoothness nor finite type of G has been used.
